item.title: George Russell explains late-race crash in Las Vegas F1 victory bid
item.description: Motorsport photo George Russell has admitted to making “a high-risk move” after crashing with three laps remaining in Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix in an attempt to clinch victory. As ‘yo-yo’ racing returned to F1, polesitter Max Verstappen and Russell frequently traded the lead throughout the race, occasionally challenged by the sister cars of Isack Hadjar in the first half of the race and Kimi Antonelli later on. On lap 48 of 50, Russell had dropped down to third behind Verstappen and Antonelli and dived down the inside of his team-mate’s Silver Arrow, but locked up and hit the wall. Minimal damage meant he was able to finish the race, albeit down in ninth. “I knew if I wanted to win the race I needed to be in second going into the last couple of laps,” the Briton explained. “Kimi didn't have the overtake mode and I just went for a high-risk move and paid the price, but I don't regret it. Of course I'm disappointed with it, but I could have been conservative and I would have finished in third.” Russell took the lead of the race away from Verstappen on at least six occasions without ever being able to hold on to it, due to the way F1’s new power units – and particularly their batteries and energy deployment – work on this high-speed street circuit. “It was interesting,” the Mercedes driver commented. “I think it was quite fun for maybe half the race. Then it started to get a bit tiring at one point because it was absolutely impossible to get away. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes “I felt I was in a very good deployment mode to overtake Verstappen and be ahead of the start line. Kimi was overtaking but Max was already re-overtaking before the line. But it left me very vulnerable in the middle sector, and that's why I lost some positions. I went down to P5, and then I had to change my strat mode, and it helped me get back up the order. “I felt into the last lap I could go back to what I had to try and win the race. It was tough.” This ‘yo-yo’ type of racing, which is reminiscent of Formula E, hadn’t been seen to this extent since the opening races of the season. “It was just learning on the fly, really,” Russell added. “Yeah, learning on the fly, it was very bizarre. The speed differences in the straight were monumental. I was gaining 1.3s on the straight on Max, it was wild. Strange race.” Russell’s lowly result means he is down to fourth in the drivers’ championship – on equal points with fifth-placed Lando Norris , three points away from Lewis Hamilton and a whopping 40 points adrift of runner-up Verstappen. item.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
item.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that saw a non-stop battle for the lead for the entire race. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps, Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Verstappen in control despite lead changes Challengers came and went but Max Verstappen was never without the lead for long in Las Vegas [Getty Images] "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. The race went on and on like that, punctuated by a mid-grand prix safety car, but through it all Verstappen always seemed in control. item.title: Jordan Love names two ‘stand-out’ Rams stars who could cause problems for Packers
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Jordan Love has identified Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald as two players who could cause serious problems for the Green Bay Packers when they face the Los Angeles Rams. The Rams have won four consecutive games and arrive at the contest fresh from a convincing 34-6 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Their defensive front is a major reason why Love believes Green Bay face a difficult challenge. However, the Packers could also receive a significant boost of their own, with Micah Parsons making progress in his recovery from a serious knee injury. Jordan Love highlights Los Angeles Rams defensive threat while Micah Parsons makes progress Asked what stands out about the Rams’ defensive front, Love immediately pointed towards Garrett and Donald. “The front, that’s what stands out to you. Obviously, Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, they got a lot of good guys up front. Especially when they’re in base, you get five one-on-one blocks. So yeah, they got some good players over there, so that definitely stands out.” Love also stressed that Green Bay must give him enough protection while creating opportunities in the running game. “Obviously, Myles has been out for a little while, but it’s something that we talk about all week. It starts up front. We gotta handle business. We gotta be able to block the front, give me some time in the run game. We gotta be able to get hands on people, create some lanes in the run game.” Meanwhile, there is encouraging news surrounding Parsons, who returned to practice after tearing his ACL and undergoing meniscus surgery in December 2025. Love was impressed by what he saw from the pass rusher, telling reporters: “You felt his presence out there and that’s what he brings to the table on a daily basis. He’s moving around really well.” Parsons has yet to play this season and Green Bay must decide whether to activate him from the physically unable to perform list. His 21-day practice window is due to close on the day of the Rams game, but his return is not guaranteed. The Packers are taking a cautious approach, with head coach Matt LaFleur making practice performances the key factor in the decision. With the Rams’ defensive front posing a major threat, having Parsons back would be a welcome boost for Green Bay. However, Love and the Packers must prepare for the possibility of facing Los Angeles without him. item.title: Wales coach Tandy frustrated by Australia defeat
item.description: Wales head coach Steve Tandy said he was frustrated as his side failed to back up their epic win over New Zealand, narrowly losing to Australia. The Wallabies edged the Nations Championship Test 29-26 in Cardiff, a week after a first Wales victory over the All Blacks since 1953 had led to wild celebrations. Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau secured a try-bonus point for Australia as Ryan Lonergan and Carter Gordon added nine points with the boot. Wales also scored four tries, through Dewi Lake's double, Blair Murray and Ryan Elias, with Sam Costelow landing three conversions. However, they fell agonisingly short. "The overarching feeling is the frustration of losing," said Tandy. "We were disappointed. We probably weren't as accurate as we could have been. We were held up three times and could have gone ahead on the scoreboard." The 46-year-old former Ospreys coach added: "Maybe we needed a little bit of composure but there were enough opportunities to come away with the win. "I know it's not the result anyone wanted but the supporters were amazing again." Despite the loss, and that frustration, the Wales head coach praised his side's attitude in attempting to follow up their historic win against the All Blacks. "Fair play to the boys, after such a monumental game last week with the emotional energy, we stuck in the game and scored four tries," he said. "So there are a lot of positives in the performance to take as well." Australia hold on for narrow win against Wales Nations Championship - Australia triumph over Wales - reaction Highs and lows of sport - Lake Dewi Lake has scored three tries in the past two internationals [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Australia, having soaked up fierce first-half pressure, produced some fine attacking rugby after the break to prevent Wales from winning three matches in a row for the first time since the 2023 World Cup. "It's sport, you have major highs and then lows, and that's the game we play," said skipper Lake. "Our frustration comes from the fact that we probably weren't at our best. "We created opportunities during large parts of the game, but there were little inaccuracies at the wrong times." Lake, however, said he could not fault the effort of the squad. "We spoke about backing up last weekend, and we didn't back it up with a result but I think we backed it up with effort and energy," said the captain. "We had opportunities to win that game, but unfortunately it wasn't to be for us today. "We'll fix those accuracy issues and we'll be ready to go again next week." Wales will face Japan at the Allianz Stadium at Twickenham on Saturday after both sides finished fifth in the two Nations Championship tables - north and south. It will be a fifth time Wales and Japan have met in 16 months with Tandy's side defeating Eddie Jones' team 28-21 in Cardiff just two weeks ago. item.title: Super Formula Suzuka: Tomoki Nojiri breaks drought with win in season finale
item.description: Motorsport photo Tomoki Nojiri ended a year-long Super Formula win drought in the final race of the season at Suzuka on Sunday, beating newly-crowned champion Kakunoshin Ohta . Team Mugen driver Nojiri converted a record-extending 26th pole into a first victory since the penultimate round of the season last year by a margin of 2.5 seconds, holding off a charge from Dandelion Racing's Ohta in the closing laps. After a relatively uneventful opening stint in which he led fellow front-row starter Nirei Fukuzumi , Nojiri completed his mandatory stop on lap 12 of 31, but encountered slower traffic as Ohta embarked on an ambitious overcut strategy. With no safety car, Ohta showed strong pace on older rubber before his stop on lap 26, but afterwards he not only slipped behind Nojiri but also the yet-to-stop Giuliano Alesi. Once clear of Alesi, Ohta rapidly cut down the eight-second advantage that Nojiri had, setting a succession of fastest laps, but was unable to catch the two-time champion. Saturday race winner and series runner-up Ayumu Iwasa completed the podium in third, but lacked the pace of team-mate Nojiri and was a distant 20.6 seconds adrift at the finish. The Red Bull Formula 1 reserve had to fend off a strong late challenge from Rookie Racing driver Fukuzumi, who slipped behind Iwasa on cold tyres as he struggled on his out lap. Ayumu Iwasa, TEAM MUGEN AUTOBACS Ayumu Iwasa, TEAM MUGEN AUTOBACS Fukuzumi was best of the Toyota drivers in fourth behind an all-Honda top three, ahead of Tadasuke Makino (Dandelion) and Kamui Kobayashi (TGM Grand Prix). Williams F1 reserve Luke Browning secured Rookie of the Year in seventh place for Kondo Racing, his best finish since May's Suzuka round. Browning made it through to Q2 for the first time of the year in dry conditions, albeit starting 12th after having his best lap deleted for track limits, but jumped to seventh on the first lap. Like Ohta, Browning elected to leave his pit stop late, until lap 29, but after slipping behind Kobayashi on his out lap he was unable to make up places on new tyres. Completing the points scorers were Cerumo/Inging drivers Sena Sakaguchi and Toshiki Oyu , who swapped places on the last lap as Sakaguchi swept around the outside at 130R, and Nakajima Racing’s Ren Sato . Nakajima Racing missed out on overhauling TOM’S for third in the teams’ standings, not helped by Fraga starting last after a mysterious electrical shutdown in qualifying. Fraga could only recover to 14th in the race, but kept hold of third in the drivers’ standings. TOM’S endured a disastrous final race of the season as Formula 2-bound Sho Tsuboi damaged his front wing after contact with Yuto Nomura’s B-Max Racing car, forcing him into an early stop for a new nose on his way to 19th place. Sacha Fenestraz meanwhile was a lowly 20th after spinning on cold tyres on his out lap and clipping Nomura, damaging his nose in the process. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: 3 Takeaways as Wembanyama's 50-point night leads Spurs past Pelicans
item.description: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) dunks against the New Orleans Pelicans during the second quarter of the NBA game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Wembanyama scored 50 points and grabbed 19 rebounds in 32 minutes as the Spurs defeated the Pelicans 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Whatever Spurs coach Mitch Johnson had drawn up for Saturday's game against New Orleans, it didn't take long for Victor Wembanyama to render it obsolete. The new game plan was considerably simpler. "Just get him the ball," forward Keldon Johnson said. The Spurs did. Wembanyama delivered. In a statistical line that has never been recorded in NBA history, Wembanyama finished with 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals to lead a dominating 114-91 victory over the Pelicans. It marked Wembanyama's second 50-point game of the season, joining a 52-point, 24-rebound effort in a Nov. 4 win over Dallas. He came within one board of making it his second 50-20 game as well. Wembanyama put up 17 points in the first quarter, a career high for a single frame. No player in the NBA this season had posted a game with at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals. Wembanyama had that by halftime. His 32 points in the first half Saturday would have been a Spurs franchise record, were it not for the 37 he put on the L.A. Lakers last season. The 22-year-old All-Star views his personal accolades as a byproduct of team success. "It just comes when we play the right way," said Wembanyama, who finished 20 of 29 from the field and 5 of 11 from 3-point distance. "I just want to stack them up, many more." Stephon Castle added 19 points and five 3-pointers for the Spurs, who improved to 9-0 this season against teams with losing records. Jeremiah Fears scored 29 points and Jordan Poole had 25 for the Pelicans, who were playing without star forward Zion Williamson (thigh contusion). New Orleans had little answer for Wembanyama, the 7-foot-4 Frenchman who transformed the Frost Bank Center into his personal playground. With Wembanyama chasing his third career 50-point game, coach Mitch Johnson allowed him to remain on the floor into the fourth quarter of an increasingly lopsided affair. San Antonio Spurs center Tarris Reed Jr. (10) and forward Harrison Barnes (40) play in the fourth quarter of an NBA game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. The Spurs won 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Wembanyama reached the half-century mark on a step-back 3-pointer with 6:30 remaining, then exited to a standing ovation. "I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did," Mitch Johnson said. "It would have been hard to take him out that close to 50." Asked if he would have had to spar with Wembanyama if he had tried to lift him with 47 points, the coach laughed. "No comment," he said. item.title: Bayern Munich president not worried about Michael Olise transfer rumors
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 20: Michael Olise of FC Bayern Munich during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between FC Bayern München and 1. FC Köln at Allianz Arena on November 20, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by F. Noever/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images It’s no surprise that Michael Olise is in high demand among top clubs across Europe’s top five leagues, but the Bayern Munich winger has not personally expressed any desire to leave the German Rekordmeister . His contract with Bayern runs through June 2029—he signed a five-year deal when he joined from Crystal Palace in the summer of 2024—and Bayern hopes to have him sign a contract extension, following in the footsteps of Dayot Upamecano and Harry Kane. With his nonchalant, relaxed manner off the pitch, Olise is not a man of many words in front of a microphone, making it hard to tell whether he is thinking about a new challenge away from Munich soon or wants to stay long-term. Right now, Bayern has not yet sat down with the player and/or his representatives for concrete discussions about his future. Even so, the club remains relaxed about his contract situation despite heavy interest from clubs like Real Madrid and Liverpool. Speaking at Bayern’s annual general meeting, club president Herbert Hainer echoed that the front office is not worried about Olise’s contract and is, for now, focused on his football. “As for all the rumors surrounding Michael, we are very relaxed. He has a contract until 2029. And let me also say something about you as a person, dear Michael. I would much rather have someone who makes a statement with the ball at his feet than someone who makes headlines with a microphone in front of him! Because the fans want genuine characters and personalities who stand out. And dear Michael, first and foremost, I wish you a speedy recovery. Don’t let anyone change you . Stay exactly as you are,” Hainer passionately said (via @iMiaSanMia ). Olise himself narrowly avoided a serious injury when a challenge from behind caused his ankle to roll and land awkwardly just before halftime in Bayern’s 1-1 draw with FC Köln on Friday evening. With an injury list that now includes Harry Kane, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, Manuel Neuer, and Luis Díaz, Vincent Kompany will be relieved that nothing too serious happened to Olise. Bayern’s attack looked noticeably different without both Kane and Olise — a testament to how much they mean to the team. Time will tell what happens with Olise, though Bayern handled the extensions for Upamecano and Kane with the same calm approach, which bodes well for talks with him. Join the conversation! item.title: Defense Carries Irish Over SMU
item.description: Notre Dame’s defense made key stops in critical moments as the Irish won by 24-3 on Senior Night. SMU’s potent offense poked holes in Notre Dame throughout the evening but failed to breach the goal line. CJ Carr and the Irish attack sputtered at times and stopped themselves with two careless turnovers. Several explosive plays were the difference in the game as Carr hit long passes to multiple receivers. The win moves Notre Dame to 10-1 on the season on a wild day of upsets in college football. item.title: 'He will see what Man Utd are made of' - Pulis on Pochettino's first game
item.description: [BBC] Stepping into a job like Mauricio Pochettino has done at Manchester United, where managers have come and gone frequently, will always lead you to wonder why the others have not lasted very long. Irrespective of results, you face these first few days in your new post with suspicion. So, while what happens in Pochettino's first game against Liverpool on Sunday is important, it will not define his early opinions of the club - good or bad. Whenever you take over a team in mid-season, which I did on a few occasions, you don't usually get much time to work with your players before your first game. Jumping straight in and going straight to the heart of a two-day preparation for a game, like Pochettino has done before United go to Anfield, is so difficult and I am not sure any manager can honestly make a profound difference. A change of voice helps, I'm sure, but so does showing strength and confidence in your own principles and making sure the players understand you demand complete and utter commitment in all the games you face, starting with this one. With time on the training ground being so limited, my initial work would focus on us being a team and working up and down the pitch together, by breaking down different scenarios inside the game and what we should do in them. I'd keep the focus on hard work and making us difficult to beat - clean sheets are so under-rated. Then, on the day, your first pre-match speech is always a massive one, and it will be the same for Pochettino too. My first team talk would always focus on generating an 'us against the world' mentality. As a manager coming in now, you've usually got the job because the team has struggled, so you can play on that to motivate the players. You can use media reports and stories to show the negativity against them - but then counter that by producing a real 'stand-up and be counted' kind of rallying call, before sending them out on the pitch, while mentioning your faith in them to succeed. The existing staff would know more about the lads' qualities in that respect than myself or anyone who had just arrived with me, so I'd always discuss that with the people I had inherited, from fitness coaches to the medical department. item.title: 'Goosebumps!' - Super-sub Carlos Espi salutes Bernabeu roar after bailing out Real Madrid against Celta
item.description: Real Madrid v RC Celta de Vigo - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Carlos Espi admitted the Santiago Bernabeu atmosphere gave him "goosebumps" after his 85th-minute rebound secured Real Madrid's 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo. The young striker stressed squad unity as Los Blancos extended their winning streak to nine matches ahead of Tuesday's Champions League battle. Espi completes late Bernabeu comeback Carlos Espi struck in the 85th minute to seal a 2-1 comeback victory for Real Madrid against Celta Vigo and extend their winning run to nine consecutive matches. After Pablo Duran gave Celta a sixth-minute lead and Kylian Mbappe blazed a first-half penalty over the crossbar, Jude Bellingham levelled on 66 minutes before Espi pounced on a rebound from Vinicius Junior's cross. The decisive finish marked the Valencian forward's fourth goal of the campaign and preserved Real Madrid's perfect home record this season. Speaking after the final whistle, Espi admitted the backing from the stands left a powerful impression on him. Match-winner reveals 'goosebumps' from crowd support Espi explained that every substitute entered the pitch determined to turn the contest around , crediting the collective spirit inside the 23-to-24-man squad alongside the vocal home crowd. "I get goosebumps," Espi said. "It's indescribable how much support I feel from everyone. I will give my all for the madridistas and for this club. I try to do what the coach asks of me, and every minute I get, I will make the most of it. If I can help the team, even better. As I said the other day, the goal is to stay united. We're 23-24 players, and we all need to move in the same direction. Those of us who came on did so fully focused on securing the victory, and that's what we achieved." Home fortress fuels ninth straight triumph While Real Madrid endured a frustrating opening half, Espi insisted dropping points at the Santiago Bernabeu was never an option once the crowd lifted the team in the second period. Full focus shifts to Tuesday's Champions League tie With only 48 hours to recover from a demanding domestic test, Espi stressed that Los Blancos must immediately channel their momentum into European action. "Now, the most important thing is Tuesday because this doesn't stop," he concluded. "We have two days to prepare for the match, and with all our enthusiasm, we're going for it."

item.title: Maple Leafs Need to Fire Jim Hiller After Latest Collapse
item.description: Jim Hiller Maple Leafs Getty The time has come for the Toronto Maple Leafs to grow some stones and fire head coach Jim Hiller. This statement isn’t some knee-jerk reaction to the team’s most recent loss. It’s a natural consequence of yet another third-period collapse. The Maple Leafs were leading 3-1 midway through the second period before three unanswered goals led to a Columbus Blue Jackets’ 4-3 win. But it was the two goals roughly a minute apart that added insult to injury. Sure, Hiller wasn’t on the ice for the two goals. He wasn’t playing in goal. He wasn’t the guy who didn’t block a shot or clear the puck from the zone. However, someone has to be accountable for the situation. Someone has to answer to the latest debacle. And as much as the players are to blame for the situation, the bottom line is that the ax has to fall somewhere, and that somewhere will be Jim Hiller’s head. Do the Maple Leafs Have Any Other Choice? While it’s easy to call for the coach’s head, the fact of the matter is: Do the Maple Leafs have any other choice? Does the organization have any other realistic path forward? Hiller doesn’t seem to have an answer for any of what’s going on. He doesn’t seem to grasp the seriousness of the situation befalling the team. Meanwhile, GM John Chayka is feeling the heat. He’s the guy responsible for hiring Hiller. That’s why one has to think that there is no other way around this. Chayka can either fess up to his mistake and try to right the wrong, or stubbornly try to wiggle his way out of the mess. It’s clear that he’s out of runway. The Maple Leafs are in a death spiral with no clear end in sight. Something has to give. Unless there’s a magic solution that no one is aware of, the Leafs don’t really have any other choice. The chain will have to break in the weakest link, and that link is Jim Hiller. Any Option Is Better Than Nothing at This Point Yes, it’s true that no move is better than a bad move. That situation applied to the Leafs a week ago. Now, that’s not the case anymore. While the goal is not to make a gut-call at this time, the fact is that something will have to change. The Maple Leafs cannot afford to let this latest mess go unanswered. It will either have to be a massive trade to really shake the team up, or it will have to be a coaching change. The latter is the easiest way out for now. It’s also worth noting that a coaching change won’t preclude a trade. Nevertheless, Chayka can’t tip his hand right now. Everyone knows he’s in a bind. So, there won’t be any compassion from any other GM out there. Let’s see what happens. The Maple Leafs next game will be on Monday night in Long Island against the Islanders. That gives the organization very little time to make a decision, if any. Regardless of the tight turnaround, there may be no other way out. item.description: Red Sox urged to sign 6-foot-9, 260-pound pitcher Bailey Ober after the Twins cut ties. Here's why the former Minnesota starter could interest Boston. Getty Bailey Ober, the 6-foot-9, 260-pound right-hander non-tendered by the Minnesota Twins Friday, is being urged for the Boston Red Sox as a one-year rotation option, in a new report by analyst Brandon Glick of BoSox Injection. With Sonny Gray returning to Minnesota as a free agent after winning 18 games for the Red Sox in his lone year with the franchise, Boston is short on right-handed starters, and BoSox Injection says the pitcher the Twins cut loose fits what the Red Sox do best. Ober, albeit flawed, matches the type of arm Boston’s pitching department under pitching coach Andrew Bailey has shown it can reshape, Glick argues. Glick points to Ober’s size and low arm slot, which disguise his pitches, and to a 7.2-foot extension that landed in the 96th percentile of the league this year. Ober was projected to earn $6.9 million in arbitration in his final year of club control, and the Twins’ rotation already includes Gray, Joe Ryan, Pablo López and Taj Bradley, with Dean Kremer added at the deadline. We lost our tracking for sure, we’re getting beat up the ice and a couple odd-man (rushes) there. And they’ll (Coachella Valley) make you pay with how much firepower they have.” Although Ontario had a four-game win streak, Coachella Valley was 3-1-0 in their last four. And the Firebirds hold a better record and standing in the AHL Pacific Division (9-6-3-1; 22 points; 4th place) in comparison to Ontario (9-8-1-0; 19 points; 8th place). Ian McKinnon scored an unassisted goal as his puck ricocheted off Portillo’s leg pad, sneaking to the back of the net and giving the Firebirds the early 1-0 lead. Avon would also help on Morrison’s insurance goal. The Firebirds would head into the final period up ahead 4-1, but there was still 20 minutes left of hockey. They were really good; out of their own zone, encountering us, and making some of those fast break plays. They kept playing all the way through and when you do that sometimes big things can happen.” And big things happened, but closing out the game did not.
